summary: Tanero Sasakawa was a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896) and later held posts at Toyo University and Meiji University.

Tansen Sen works in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, later serving at Baruch College (1997–2017) and NYU Shanghai (Professor, 2017).
Tanso Hirose was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied at Kamei Juku (~1797–1801) and under Hōdō, and he founded Kangien in 1801.

Tanuja Ajotikar specializes in Indology and computational linguistics. She held posts at Harvard University and Maharishi Vedic University, and served as Assistant Professor at the Sanskrit Library (attested 2024–2025).

Tanzan Hara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Yushima Seido and Shoheizaka Gakumonjo. He taught at the University of Tokyo (1879) and served as superintendent at Komazawa University (1891).
Tao Chen is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (2017–2026). In 2026, he was appointed a postdoctoral fellow at Fo Guang Shan.

Tao Jiang specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Rutgers University (attested 2011).
Tao Jin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed a PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2008 under Alexander L. Mayer.
Tao Pan is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He earned a BA at Fudan University in 2010 and completed a Magister Artium at the University of Munich.

Tara Doyle is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. At Emory University, she served as a lecturer and director of the Tibetan Studies Program (attested 2003) and later as Professor Emerita (attested 2026).
Tarapada Chowdhury was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Edward Hamilton Johnston by 1950 and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Patna College (attested 1950).
Tara Sheemar specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned a PhD from Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2011 and became an Associate Professor at Janki Devi Memorial College in 2003.
Tarab Tulku was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a curator at the Royal Danish Library (~1962–2000) and held a post at the University of Copenhagen (~1963–1998).

Taranatha Tarkavachaspati was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor of Grammar and Philosophy at Sanskrit College and University (~1845–1872) and as Professor of Sanskrit at Benares Sanskrit College.

Tariq Rafeeq Khan is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He earned a PhD from Jiwaji University (2017–2020) and became an assistant professor at the Islamic University of Science and Technology in 2022.

Taro Tokutake is an Indologist and historian who earned his BA at Hiroshima University and PhD at Kyoto University. He taught at Kyoto University (2024) and held visiting postdoctoral fellowships at CNRS (2024–2025), Paris Cité (2025–2026), and Edinburgh (2026).

Tarthang Tulku is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Tarthang Monastery, held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1962–1968) and the Tibetan Nyingma Meditation Center (~1969), and founded the Nyingma Institute in 1972.
Tashi Densapa was a Tibetology and history scholar. He served as editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1978, 2002) and as director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 2008).

Tashi Rabgey is a scholar of Tibetology who studied at University College Toronto, Magdalen College, Cambridge, and Harvard. She held posts at Georgetown University and the University of Virginia (~2008–2011).

Tashi Samphel works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as director of the Songtsen Library (attested 2015) and as Associate Professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).
